topic.title: How a bank earns on the gap between what it pays a saver and what it charges a borrower

title: Your bank pays you almost nothing. Here's why 🏦
description:
Does your bank really keep your money for free? Follow one saver's deposit to a borrower, and see what JPMorgan earned on the gap in 2025.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Did you know your bank did this? Comment

lines.text: Your money, held for free? Watch this.
Rohan's savings earn him $50 a year from his bank.
His bank lends that money to Priya, who pays $700.
So the bank keeps the difference. But that's only one account.
And JPMorgan's whole gap last year? Look at this.
Every single day, that gap brings the bank this much money.
So was your money ever free? It was rented out.

notes: 26 figures computed from inputs; 20 cross-checked against closed-form formulas.

New turn 'Every single day, that gap brings the bank this much money' shows $261.5M (A day) = $95.44B / 365 from maths day citing fact 1: a true daily average of 2025 NII; jpm headline still shows $95.44B as 'Interest in, minus interest paid out, one year'. Hook 'Your money, held for free?' and payoff 'It was rented out' are fair simplifications. Unsupported profit comparison is gone. Realistic illustrative rates, no advice, disclaimer ends description. Notes: $261.5M is an average (could be 'on average'); 'keeps the difference' ignores costs/defaults; description lacks licensed-adviser line.
